skill.name: agentspace
skill.description: Share a user-selected local file or folder through an Agentspace browser workspace using the ascli command-line tool.
skill.summary: Create a browser-accessible workspace for a selected local path and return its share link.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: The pipe-to-shell and reconnaissance alerts are false positives because the reference explicitly prohibits curl-to-shell installation and restricts operations to named paths. The skill still directs agents to execute a third-party CLI, install a mutable package version, and upload selected files to anonymous workspaces with optional edit access. No prompt injection attempt or covert collection outside the selected path was found.

remediation.issue: Anonymous editable sharing can expose or alter local artifacts.
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation of the exact path, permission, recipients, and expiration before upload. Default to view-only access and a short expiration.

remediation.issue: The workflow installs or executes the mutable @latest npm package.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed package version and integrity value. Request explicit approval before installation or first execution, and avoid global installation by default.

remediation.issue: User-supplied paths are shown as shell placeholders without argument-handling guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Pass paths as separate process arguments or apply robust shell quoting. Confirm ambiguous paths and reject unintended option-like values.

content.user_title: Share Agent Workspaces in a Browser
content.value_statement: Local agent artifacts are difficult to review from another device or with teammates. Agentspace uploads a selected path and returns a browser link for viewing, comments, or editing.
actual_capabilities: Shares one explicitly selected local file or folder through ascli.
Creates an anonymous workspace and returns the link printed by the CLI.
Supports view-only or edit permissions for shared workspaces.
Supports a 24-hour expiration option for temporary sharing.
Runs through an installed ascli command or the published npx package.
Checks the binding status of a selected path.
limitations: Requires an existing ascli installation or Node.js with npm, plus network access to agentspace.so.
Anonymous workspaces expire after 24 hours unless claimed by email.
Uploads the selected local content to a third-party hosted service.
Anyone with a share link may access content according to its assigned permission.

use_cases.title: Review Generated Artifacts Remotely
use_cases.description: Share generated code, reports, screenshots, or build logs for browser review from another device.

use_cases.title: Collect View-Only Feedback
use_cases.description: Create a temporary view-only workspace for test evidence or project outputs without sending an archive.

use_cases.title: Hand Off an Editable Workspace
use_cases.description: Share a selected project folder with edit access so a teammate can continue work in the browser.

prompt_templates.title: Share One File
prompt_templates.prompt: Share the file at [exact path] with view-only access. Confirm the path before uploading, then return the CLI-generated link.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single artifact

prompt_templates.title: Share a Project Folder
prompt_templates.prompt: Share [exact folder path] for 24 hours with view-only permission. State the selected path and permission before running the command.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Editable Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an editable Agentspace workspace for [exact path]. Confirm that the folder excludes secrets and return only the generated share URL.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Safe Sharing Method
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether ascli is available. If absent, propose a pinned npx command and request approval before sharing [exact path] as view-only.

output_examples.output: Confirmed path: /work/demo/report.pdf. Permission: view-only. I returned the exact temporary workspace link produced by Agentspace.

output_examples.input: Hand off /work/demo to my teammate with edit access.
output_examples.output: Confirmed path: /work/demo. Permission: edit. I shared the folder and returned the exact URL printed by the CLI.
Which exact folder path should I share, and should recipients have view-only or edit access?

best_practices: Confirm the exact path and inspect selected contents for secrets before uploading.
Default to view-only access and the shortest practical expiration.
Return only the exact workspace URL printed by the CLI.
anti_patterns: Do not share the current directory when the requested path is ambiguous.
Do not upload credentials, environment files, private keys, or unrelated personal data.
Do not install or execute an unreviewed mutable package without explicit approval.

faq.question: What does this skill share?
faq.answer: It shares one local file or folder that the user explicitly identifies.

faq.question: Does sharing require an account?
faq.answer: No account is required for an anonymous workspace. The skill states that claiming by email keeps a workspace permanent.

faq.question: Which permissions are available?
faq.answer: The documented commands support view-only and edit permissions.

faq.question: How long does an anonymous workspace remain available?
faq.answer: The skill states that anonymous workspaces remain available for 24 hours.

faq.question: What software is required?
faq.answer: Use an existing ascli command or Node.js with npm or npx. Network access is also required.

faq.question: Where is shared data sent?
faq.answer: The skill states that traffic goes only to agentspace.so and uses Cloudflare hosting. The service implementation is not included for verification.
